summary.en-US: Read web pages and PDFs aloud with natural open-source neural voices (Kokoro, MOSS-TTS) that run on your own computer. Needs the free r-aloud local server.

description.en-US: r-aloud reads web pages, selections and PDFs aloud using open-source neural text-to-speech that runs entirely on your own machine. Nothing is sent to a cloud service. Important: r-aloud needs its companion TTS server running locally (Linux): https://github.com/AvAkanksh/r-aloud — run ./install.sh --server-only. Features: - Read the whole page (main article detected) or just your selection - Highlights the sentence being read and follows it - PDF reader for local and web PDFs, with selection reading and "read from here" - Floating mini-player, popup controls, right-click menu, keyboard shortcuts (Alt+Shift+R read/pause, Alt+Shift+X stop) - About 50 Kokoro voices in 9 languages; change voice or speed mid-read - Optional MOSS-TTS-Realtime engine with voice cloning on a capable GPU Privacy: page text goes only to the server on 127.0.0.1. No analytics, no tracking.
